title: Last-night checklist
examples: Should I study right before the exam?
How much sleep do I really need for a big test?
What is the best way to review notes quickly?

explain.say: Today we are learning about a last night checklist for studying.

items: Prepare all your books and pens
Aim for a good amount of sleep
Do a light review of your notes

explain.say: First we need to check our equipment before we start studying.
Next we must think about getting enough restful sleep tonight.
Our third step is to do a light review of what you have already learned.
For a real life example imagine you are going to take a science test.
A common mistake is trying to learn too much right before bed.

faq.q: How long before the test should I stop studying?
faq.a: It is best to stop studying at least one hour before you plan to sleep. This helps your brain wind down properly for rest.
asks: What is the ideal time to stop studying?

faq.q: Is reading my notes the same as actually practicing questions?
faq.a: No, reading notes is passive. You should try to practice answering questions to test what you actually remember.
asks: Should I just read my textbook?

faq.q: What if I feel really anxious the night before?
faq.a: If you feel anxious, focus on the things you already know well. A short, calm review is better than panicking over new topics.
asks: How do I calm down before the exam?
What should I do if I feel stressed?

faq.q: Do I need special pens or colored highlighters?
faq.a: You do not need special items. Just having all the standard equipment like pens and pencils ready is the most important part.
asks: What kind of pens should I use?

faq.q: Does exercise help with memory the night before?
faq.a: Light physical activity can help keep you alert, but avoid anything too intense right before bed. Gentle movement is better.
asks: Is a walk okay before bed?

facts: Getting enough sleep helps your brain move information from short-term to long-term memory.
A light review means looking over topics, not trying to learn entirely new material.
Having all your stationery ready saves time and reduces morning stress.
Staying calm is more helpful than cramming facts right before an assessment.

quiz.say: To prepare for a test, what is the most important thing to do the night before?
quiz.show: A) Study new chapters all night.

options.show: A) Study new chapters all night.
options.say: A) Study new chapters all night.

quiz.why: Gathering your equipment ensures you can start revising immediately without searching for things.

wrong.0: This causes burnout and prevents your brain from consolidating what you already know.
wrong.1: Reading summaries is good, but you must also check that all your tools are ready to use.
wrong.2: Videos can be distracting and are not as effective as reviewing your own organized notes.

quiz.say: If you are reviewing notes, what should you focus on doing?

options.show: B) Reading over the whole textbook.
options.say: B) Reading over the whole textbook.

options.show: C) Testing yourself with practice questions.
options.say: C) Testing yourself with practice questions.

quiz.why: Testing yourself forces your brain to retrieve the memory, which is the best way to check what you know.

wrong.0: Reading everything is overwhelming and wastes time on things you already know well.
wrong.1: Making new materials takes too much energy when you should be resting.
wrong.3: This is slow and does not prove you can recall the information under pressure.

quiz.say: Which action best supports memory consolidation?
quiz.show: A) Staying up late to read.

options.show: A) Staying up late to read.
options.say: A) Staying up late to read.

options.show: C) Doing intense revision right up to bedtime.
options.say: C) Doing intense revision right up to bedtime.

quiz.why: Sleep is when your brain organizes and saves the information you learned during the day.

wrong.0: Lack of sleep severely impairs your ability to recall facts the next day.
wrong.1: This keeps your mind too active, making it harder for you to fall into deep, restful sleep.
wrong.2: A balanced approach that includes rest is more effective than focusing on just one area.
